courses.title: English 11 – American Literature
courses.description: A chronological survey of American literature from Puritan writing through contemporary voices, read alongside the founding documents and speeches that shaped the nation. Students write rhetorical analyses, literary arguments, a personal narrative suitable for college applications, and a sustained research paper, with grammar and vocabulary woven into each week. Seminars and recitations build formal speaking skills.

standards.RI.11-12.6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective.

units.title: Puritan and Colonial Voices
units.big_idea: Early American writing reveals how faith, fear, and community shaped a new society—and how drama can use that past to critique the present.

units.title: The Rhetoric of Revolution
units.big_idea: The founders used persuasion and reasoned argument to justify independence and define American ideals.

units.title: Romanticism and Transcendentalism
units.big_idea: American Romantics celebrated the individual, nature, and intuition while Dark Romantics probed sin and the irrational.

units.title: Voices of Freedom: Slavery and Civil War
units.big_idea: Enslaved and free Americans used narrative and oratory to claim the nation's promise of liberty.

units.title: Realism and Regionalism
units.big_idea: After the Civil War, writers turned to ordinary lives, local speech, and the gap between ideals and reality.

units.title: Modernism and the Harlem Renaissance
units.big_idea: Modern writers fractured old forms to capture disillusionment, the city, and the search for identity and the American Dream.

units.title: The Research Paper
units.big_idea: Sustained research means asking a real question, weighing sources, and building an original argument with honest citation.

units.title: Mid-Century America: Drama and Civil Rights
units.big_idea: Postwar drama and civil rights rhetoric tested whether the American Dream was open to all.

units.title: Contemporary and Diverse American Voices
units.big_idea: Contemporary writers expand who tells the American story, exploring language, memory, war, and belonging.

units.title: Synthesis and Final Portfolio
units.big_idea: Revisiting the year's texts shows how American literature argues with itself across centuries.

days.work: Write a paragraph on how Miller's stage directions shape Proctor before he speaks.

days.title: Act II

days.title: Review & check

weeks.topic: The Crucible, Acts III–IV and literary argument

days.title: Act IV

days.title: Essay drafting
days.work: Write a 700-word literary argument: Is John Proctor a tragic hero? Include a counterclaim; edit for subject-verb agreement.

days.title: Aphorisms

days.work: Read 'Remarks Concerning the Savages of North America'; identify verbal irony and its target.

days.work: Track one personal virtue for three days Franklin-style and draft a 400-word reflective explanation.

objectives: Analyze rhetorical structure of founding documents
Evaluate reasoning in seminal U.S. texts

Patrick Henry, Speech to the Virginia Convention

days.title: Declaration structure

days.title: Evaluating reasoning

days.title: Review & check

weeks.topic: Rhetorical analysis essay: voices excluded and included
objectives: Write a full rhetorical analysis essay
Analyze Wheatley and Adams as counter-voices

days.title: Wheatley

days.title: Abigail Adams

days.title: Essay plan
days.work: Choose one founding-era text and outline a rhetorical analysis essay (situation, choices, effect).

days.title: Draft & edit

days.title: Unit check

objectives: Identify characteristics of Romanticism and Gothic fiction

days.work: Take notes on Romantic traits; read 'The Devil and Tom Walker' and mark satire of greed.

days.title: Poe's narrator
days.work: Read 'The Tell-Tale Heart'; annotate evidence the narrator is unreliable and chart sentence length vs. tension.

days.title: House of Usher
days.work: Read 'The Fall of the House of Usher'; trace setting as a symbol of Roderick's mind.

days.title: Structure
days.work: Write an analytical paragraph on how Poe's choice of ending structure produces 'unity of effect'.

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Determine central ideas of Transcendentalist essays
materials: Thoreau, Walden ('Where I Lived...') and 'Civil Disobedience'

days.title: Emerson
days.work: Read excerpts of 'Self-Reliance'; select five aphorisms and explain each in plain language.

days.title: Nature
days.work: Read the 'transparent eyeball' passage from 'Nature'; take a 20-minute solo nature walk and write a journal entry in imitation.

days.title: Walden
days.work: Read 'Where I Lived, and What I Lived For'; list Thoreau's arguments for simplicity and test one against your own daily schedule.

days.title: Civil Disobedience
days.work: Read excerpts; trace how Thoreau refines the term 'government' and connect to later activists.

days.title: Seminar & check
days.work: Socratic seminar: 'Would Thoreau approve of smartphones?'; write a 300-word argument response.

weeks.assessment: Seminar participation rubric and short argument.

objectives: Compare Romantic and Dark Romantic views of human nature
materials: Hawthorne, 'Young Goodman Brown' and 'The Minister's Black Veil'

days.title: Young Goodman Brown
days.work: Read and annotate symbols (Faith's ribbons, staff, forest); decide whether the journey was a dream.

days.title: Black Veil
days.work: Read 'The Minister's Black Veil'; chart the community's reactions and explain the veil's meaning in a paragraph.

days.title: Bartleby I
days.work: Read the first half of 'Bartleby'; analyze the narrator's attitude and the phrase 'I would prefer not to'.

days.title: Bartleby II
days.work: Finish the story; compare Bartleby's refusal to Thoreau's civil disobedience in a T-chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Timed essay (40 min): How do two Dark Romantic texts challenge Emerson's optimism?

weeks.topic: Poetry of a new nation: Whitman and Dickinson
objectives: Analyze form and style in poetry
materials: Whitman, 'Song of Myself' sections 1, 6, 52 and 'I Hear America Singing'
Dickinson, 'Because I could not stop for Death', 'Hope is the thing with feathers', 'Tell all the truth but tell it slant'

days.title: Whitman
days.work: Read 'Song of Myself' sections aloud; identify catalogs and anaphora and their effect.

days.title: Dickinson
days.work: Read four Dickinson poems; scan meter, mark dashes and slant rhymes, and paraphrase each.

days.title: Comparison
days.work: Plan a comparison of how Whitman and Dickinson treat death or the self; collect six quotations.

days.title: Write
days.work: Draft a 600-word poetry comparison essay, then memorize and recite one poem (12+ lines).

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Submit revised essay and take the Unit 3 test on Romantic and Transcendentalist texts.

weeks.topic: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, Ch. 1–6
objectives: Analyze how Douglass develops central ideas

days.title: Context & preface

days.title: Ch. 2–4

days.work: Analyze one paragraph's diction and syntax (balanced sentences, antithesis) in a 300-word response.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Reading quiz Ch. 1–6 and central-idea tracker check.

objectives: Compare male and female slave narratives
materials: Harriet Jacobs, Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl excerpts (Gutenberg)

days.title: Ch. 10

days.title: Ch. 11 & Appendix

days.title: Harriet Jacobs
days.work: Read the 'loophole of retreat' excerpt; compare Jacobs' appeals to women readers with Douglass' appeals.

days.title: Discussion & check
days.work: Recorded discussion comparing the two narratives; written exit response on structure.

Sojourner Truth, 'Ain't I a Woman?' (both versions)

days.title: Sojourner Truth

days.title: Review & check

weeks.assessment: Speech delivery rubric and timed rhetorical analysis.

objectives: Write an evidence-based argument synthesizing multiple texts

days.title: Prompt & claim

days.title: Outline

days.title: Draft

days.title: Revise

days.title: Unit check

days.work: Notes on Realism vs. Romanticism; read 'The Jumping Frog' (a California story) and identify the frame narrative.

objectives: Analyze how authors develop and relate story elements

days.work: Read 'Owl Creek Bridge'; diagram the three-part structure and analyze the manipulation of time.

days.title: Gilman
days.work: Read 'The Yellow Wallpaper'; track the narrator's changing descriptions of the wallpaper.

days.title: London

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a 600-word explanatory essay on how two of these authors use structure to create a surprise ending.

days.work: Build a literary-period timeline (Puritan to Realism) with two texts, traits, and a key quotation per period.

days.title: Practice passages

days.title: Writing review
days.work: Revise the weakest essay of the semester using teacher comments; write a reflection on growth.

days.title: Semester exam I

days.work: Read 'Mending Wall' and 'The Road Not Taken'; argue about the commonly misread meaning of the 'road' poem.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on Modernist traits and a short poetry explication of an unseen Frost poem.

Connect art to the Great Migration

materials: public library databases (e.g., JSTOR free articles, Gale via library card)

days.title: Choose a topic
days.work: Brainstorm topics linking an American author to historical context; narrow to an arguable research question.

days.title: Library databases
days.work: Use public library databases to locate at least six sources, including two scholarly articles.

days.title: Evaluate sources
days.work: Apply the CRAAP test to each source and discard weak ones.

days.title: Annotated bibliography
days.work: Write MLA 9 entries with 3-sentence annotations for five sources.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit research question, working thesis, and annotated bibliography for feedback.

days.title: Note-taking
days.work: Take notes using quotation, paraphrase, and summary, labeling each with source and page.

days.title: Paraphrase practice
days.work: Practice paraphrasing three tricky passages and compare with originals to avoid patchwriting.

days.title: Outline
days.work: Build a detailed outline with thesis, sub-claims, and assigned evidence.

days.title: Draft I
days.work: Draft introduction and first two body sections (about 1,000 words) with signal phrases and in-text citations.

days.title: Draft II & check
days.work: Draft remaining sections and conclusion; submit full rough draft (1,800–2,200 words).

days.title: Revision for argument
days.work: Reverse-outline the draft; revise so each paragraph advances the thesis.

days.title: Line editing

days.title: Presentation
days.work: Create a 6-minute presentation of findings with visuals and practice delivery.

days.title: Final & present
days.work: Submit final research paper and deliver the presentation with Q&A.

weeks.assessment: Final research paper and presentation rubrics.

courses.description: Algebra II extends the function families of Algebra I to polynomial, rational, radical, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, and introduces complex numbers, sequences and series, and statistical inference. Each unit pairs procedural fluency with modeling tasks drawn from real data, consistent with the 2023 California Mathematics Framework's emphasis on big ideas and data science. Graphing technology (Desmos) is used throughout.

units.title: Functions, Transformations, and Systems
units.big_idea: Every function family can be moved and stretched the same ways, and systems model competing constraints.

units.title: Quadratic Functions and Complex Numbers
units.big_idea: Quadratics can be written in forms that reveal different features, and complex numbers complete their solutions.

units.title: Polynomial Functions
units.big_idea: Polynomials behave like integers: they can be factored, divided, and their zeros determine their graphs.

units.title: Rational Expressions and Functions
units.big_idea: Rational functions are quotients of polynomials whose restrictions create asymptotes and holes.

units.title: Radical Functions, Rational Exponents, and Inverses
units.big_idea: Radicals and rational exponents are two notations for the same idea, and inverses undo functions.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.big_idea: Exponential functions model constant-percent change, and logarithms are the tool to solve for the exponent.

units.title: Trigonometric Functions
units.big_idea: The unit circle extends trigonometry to all real numbers and lets us model periodic phenomena.

units.title: Sequences and Series
units.big_idea: Patterns of repeated addition or multiplication can be written recursively, explicitly, and summed.

units.title: Statistics and Inference
units.big_idea: Randomization and variability let us draw conclusions about populations and treatments from samples.

units.title: Modeling Capstone and Final Exam
units.big_idea: Choosing the right function family is the heart of mathematical modeling.

courses.title: Physics of the Universe
courses.description: The third course of California's high school three-course NGSS model, Physics of the Universe connects motion, forces, energy, electromagnetism, and waves to Earth's interior, the Sun, stars, and the origin of the universe. Every unit is anchored in a phenomenon (a car crash, the San Andreas Fault, a solar panel, the night sky) and includes hands-on labs with household materials, PhET simulations, and engineering design challenges. Students keep a lab notebook and write claim-evidence-reasoning explanations.
courses.framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (HS Physical and Earth & Space Sciences, Engineering Design); 2016 California Science Framework – Physics of the Universe (three-course model)

courses.title: U.S. History & Geography: Continuity and Change in the Twentieth Century
courses.description: Following the California HSS Framework for grade 11, this course briefly reviews the nation's founding and nineteenth-century transformations, then studies the twentieth century in depth: industrialization and Progressivism, America's rise as a world power, the 1920s, the Depression and New Deal, World War II, the Cold War, the civil rights movements, and contemporary America. Students analyze primary sources each week (from the Library of Congress, National Archives/DocsTeach, and Calisphere), write document-based essays, and complete a National History Day–style research project. California's role (immigration, agriculture, Japanese American incarceration, aerospace, the Chicano and farmworker movements) is emphasized throughout.
courses.framework: California History–Social Science Content Standards (Grade 11); 2016 California History–Social Science Framework

standards.11.1.3: Understand the history of the Constitution after 1787 with emphasis on federal versus state authority and growing democratization.

standards.11.2.2: Describe the changing landscape, including the growth of cities linked by industry and trade, and the development of cities divided by race, ethnicity, and class.

standards.11.3.2: Analyze the great religious revivals and the leaders involved in them, including the First and Second Great Awakenings and the Civil War revivals.

units.title: Industrialization, Immigration, and Urbanization

units.big_idea: Reformers used government to tame industrial problems while the U.S. expanded its power overseas.

units.title: World War I and the 1920s

units.title: The Great Depression and the New Deal
units.big_idea: Economic collapse led Americans to accept a permanently larger role for the federal government.

units.big_idea: Total war mobilized every part of American society, tested constitutional rights at home, and made the U.S. a superpower.

units.title: The Civil Rights Movements

units.title: Contemporary America

courses.title: Spanish IV
courses.description: Spanish IV moves students toward Intermediate Mid–High proficiency through thematic units modeled on the AP Spanish Language and Culture themes: personal and public identities, families and communities, science and technology, beauty and aesthetics, contemporary life, global challenges, and Hispanic literature. Students read and listen to authentic sources daily, hold sustained conversations, write formal essays and emails, and give presentations, while mastering advanced grammar (imperfect subjunctive, si clauses, perfect tenses, passive voice). Spanish is the language of instruction.
courses.framework: 2019 California World Languages Standards (Intermediate Mid target); 2020 California World Languages Framework

standards.WL-COMM1-IM: Interpretive communication (Intermediate Mid): understand main ideas and many details in authentic texts, audio, and video on familiar and some unfamiliar topics.
standards.WL-COMM2-IM: Interpersonal communication (Intermediate Mid): sustain spontaneous conversations and written exchanges, asking and answering questions on a range of topics.
standards.WL-COMM3-IM: Presentational communication (Intermediate Mid): present information, narrate, and describe in connected sentences and paragraphs across time frames.
standards.WL-COMM4-IM: Settings for communication: use the language in real-world settings beyond the classroom, including digital communities.
standards.WL-COMM5-IM: Receptivity: recognize and use culturally appropriate gestures, register (tú/usted), and strategies to negotiate meaning.
standards.WL-COMM6-IM: Language comparisons: compare linguistic structures (e.g., subjunctive, aspect) of Spanish and English to deepen understanding of both.
standards.WL-CULT1-IM: Cultures: investigate, explain, and reflect on the relationship between practices, products, and perspectives of Spanish-speaking cultures.
standards.WL-CULT2-IM: Cultural comparisons: compare products, practices, and perspectives of Spanish-speaking cultures with one's own.
standards.WL-CONN1-IM: Connections: build, reinforce, and expand knowledge of other disciplines (history, science, art, literature) through Spanish.

courses.subject: VAPA
courses.title: Theatre & Performing Arts
courses.description: A year-long introduction to theatre as both art form and craft. Students build ensemble and improvisation skills, train voice and body, learn Stanislavski-based acting technique through monologues and scenes, survey theatre history from ancient Greece to contemporary American and Latinx theatre, explore technical design, write and devise original short plays, and culminate in a directed one-act production for a live audience. Students keep a performance journal and write formal play critiques.
courses.framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools – Theatre (High School Proficient); 2020 California Arts Education Framework

standards.TH:Cr1.1.HSI: Apply basic research to construct ideas about the visual composition of a drama/theatre work; explore physical, vocal, and physiological choices to develop a performance.
standards.TH:Cr2.1.HSI: Explore the function of history and culture in the development of a dramatic concept through a critical analysis of original ideas; investigate collaborative roles.
standards.TH:Cr3.1.HSI: Practice and revise a devised or scripted drama/theatre work using theatrical staging conventions; refine technical design choices.
standards.TH:Pr4.1.HSI: Examine how character relationships assist in telling the story; shape character choices using given circumstances.
standards.TH:Pr5.1.HSI: Practice various acting techniques to expand skills in a rehearsal or performance; use researched technical elements to increase the impact of design.
standards.TH:Pr6.1.HSI: Perform a scripted drama/theatre work for a specific audience.
standards.TH:Re7.1.HSI: Respond to what is seen, felt, and heard in a drama/theatre work to develop criteria for artistic choices.
standards.TH:Re8.1.HSI: Analyze and compare artistic choices developed from personal experiences and cultural contexts in multiple drama/theatre works.
standards.TH:Re9.1.HSI: Examine a drama/theatre work using supporting evidence and criteria while considering art forms, history, culture, and other disciplines.
standards.TH:Cn10.1.HSI: Investigate how cultural perspectives, community ideas, and personal beliefs impact a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cn11.1.HSI: Explore how cultural, global, and historic belief systems affect creative choices in a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cn11.2.HSI: Research how other theatre artists apply creative processes to tell stories in a devised or scripted drama/theatre work, using theatre research methods.

objectives: Use dramatic structure in original writing

days.title: Structure
days.work: Map Freytag's pyramid onto Trifles, labeling the inciting incident, turning points, and climax.

days.title: Dialogue only
days.work: Write a 1-page scene using only dialogue in which two characters want the same object; no stage directions allowed.

days.title: Play format
days.work: Learn standard play format (character names, parentheticals, stage directions) and reformat your scene.

days.title: Character design

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit a 3-page scene draft putting the two characters in conflict.

objectives: Write and revise a complete ten-minute play

days.title: Idea
days.work: Brainstorm 10 premises from personal, family, or community stories; pick one with a clear conflict and a single setting.

days.title: Outline
days.work: Outline the play in 6–8 beats with the turning point placed around minute 7.

days.title: Draft

days.title: Table read
days.work: Hold a table read with family or friends, recording it and noting where listeners lost interest.

days.title: Revise

objectives: Collaboratively create a devised piece from source material

days.title: Devising companies

days.title: Source gathering
days.work: Interview two community members on a shared theme (e.g., 'home') and collect found text.

days.title: Viewpoints
days.work: Explore Viewpoints (tempo, spatial relationship, repetition) to generate movement material.

days.title: Composition
days.work: Combine verbatim lines and movement into three short compositions.

days.title: Showing
days.work: Shape the compositions into a 6–8 minute piece and show it for feedback.

objectives: Present original work in a staged reading

days.title: Casting & rehearsal
days.work: Cast your ten-minute play with family/friends and rehearse it as a staged reading.

days.title: Polish
days.work: Refine stage-direction reading and transitions; finalize the devised piece.

days.title: Festival
days.work: Present the staged reading and devised piece to an audience.

days.title: Talkback
days.work: Lead a talkback using Liz Lerman's Critical Response Process and record feedback.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a 400-word reflection on what you learned as a playwright and deviser.

weeks.topic: The director's role and play selection
objectives: Select and analyze a one-act play
materials: public-domain one-acts (e.g., Glaspell's Trifles, Chekhov's The Proposal, Wilde excerpts)

days.title: The director
days.work: Read about the history of the director and watch an interview with a working director.

days.title: Selection
days.work: Read three public-domain one-acts and choose one for production, considering cast size and audience.

days.title: Script analysis
days.work: Analyze the chosen play's structure, characters, and themes in a prompt book.

days.title: Concept
days.work: Write a director's concept statement linking to the design concept from Unit 7.

days.title: Casting
days.work: Hold auditions with family/friends or a homeschool co-op and post a cast list.

days.title: Stage areas
days.work: Review stage areas and blocking notation; mark the floor plan with tape.

days.title: Pre-block
days.work: Pre-block the first half of the play in the prompt book.

days.title: Rehearsal 1
days.work: Block the first half with actors, adjusting for sightlines.

days.title: Rehearsal 2
days.work: Block the second half and record blocking in the prompt book.

days.title: Run
days.work: Hold a stumble-through of the full play and give notes.

days.title: Schedule
days.work: Build a rehearsal schedule to performance week with an off-book deadline.

days.title: Character work
days.work: Lead an actor workshop on objectives for each character.

days.title: Scene work
days.work: Work two key scenes for pacing and stakes.

days.title: Off-book run
days.work: Hold the off-book run and track line errors.

days.title: Notes
days.work: Practice giving specific, actionable notes and write a rehearsal report.

materials: set pieces, costumes, lights, sound from Unit 7 designs

days.title: Build
days.work: Build or gather the set, props, and costumes from the design portfolio.

days.title: Cue-to-cue
days.work: Run a cue-to-cue rehearsal for lights and sound.

days.title: Costume parade
days.work: Hold a costume parade and fix problems.

days.title: Tech run
days.work: Run the play with all technical elements.

days.title: Notes
days.work: Write production notes and fix issues.

objectives: Perform a one-act production for a live audience

days.title: Dress rehearsal 1
days.work: Run the full play in costume with timing notes.

days.title: Dress rehearsal 2
days.work: Final dress with an invited preview audience.

days.title: Performance 1
days.work: Perform the one-act for an audience.

days.title: Performance 2
days.work: Perform a second time and record it.

days.title: Strike
days.work: Strike the set and return materials.

days.title: Video review
days.work: Watch the production video and log strengths and growth areas.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Write a 600-word self-critique of the production using theatre criteria.

days.title: Artistic statement
days.work: Write an artistic statement about what theatre means to you.

days.title: Portfolio
days.work: Assemble a digital portfolio with headshot, résumé, monologue video, design work, and play.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take a written final on theatre terms, history, and production roles.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: Lifetime Fitness
courses.description: Lifetime Fitness (CA high school Course 3 level) prepares students to stay active for life. Students assess their own fitness, design and carry out progressive cardio, strength, and flexibility programs, and build skill in lifetime activities such as pickleball, badminton, hiking and orienteering, dance, and yoga. Classroom components cover training science, nutrition, stress management, and evaluating fitness products, ending with a personal 5-year fitness plan.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards (High School Course 3); 2009 California Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-HS3-1.1: Demonstrate proficient movement skills in at least two lifetime individual or dual activities (e.g., racquet sports, golf, hiking).
standards.PE-HS3-1.2: Demonstrate proficient movement skills in outdoor or aquatic activities and in rhythmic/dance activities.
standards.PE-HS3-1.3: Analyze and apply biomechanical principles (force, leverage, stability) to improve performance of complex skills.
standards.PE-HS3-1.4: Apply offensive, defensive, and cooperative strategies in team and dual activities.
standards.PE-HS3-2.1: Participate in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity at least four days per week and meet health-related fitness standards.
standards.PE-HS3-2.2: Assess personal levels of health-related fitness (aerobic capacity, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, body composition) and interpret results.
standards.PE-HS3-2.3: Apply the FITT principle, overload, specificity, and progression to design and implement a personal fitness program.
standards.PE-HS3-2.4: Explain and apply safe resistance-training techniques and the physiological effects of training.
standards.PE-HS3-2.5: Monitor intensity using heart rate and perceived exertion and adjust training accordingly.
standards.PE-HS3-2.6: Explain the relationships among nutrition, rest, physical activity, and long-term health, and evaluate fitness products and claims.
standards.PE-HS3-3.1: Identify and apply strategies for maintaining lifelong physical activity, including overcoming barriers and using community resources.
standards.PE-HS3-3.2: Analyze how physical activity reduces stress and improves mental and emotional health.
standards.PE-HS3-3.3: Demonstrate responsible leadership, sportsmanship, and safe practices, including officiating and risk management.
standards.PE-HS3-3.4: Set, monitor, and evaluate personal goals for physical activity and fitness.

days.title: Course launch & PACER prep

days.title: Flexibility

days.title: Body composition & activity log

days.title: Interpret results

weeks.topic: SMART goals and the FITT principle

days.title: FITT

days.title: Training principles
days.work: Learn overload, progression, specificity, and reversibility; complete an interval walk/jog.

days.title: Barriers

days.title: Check

days.title: Cool-down

days.title: Heat safety

days.title: Design

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform your routines with correct form and pass a safety quiz.

days.title: Target zones

days.title: Pulse checks

days.title: Zone training

days.title: Intervals
days.work: Perform jump-rope intervals (30 sec on/30 off ×10) and graph heart rate recovery.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on heart rate calculation and submit the heart-rate graph.

days.title: Run form
days.work: Learn running form (posture, arm swing, cadence ~170 steps/min) with drills.

days.title: Base run

days.title: Cross-training
days.work: Cycle, swim, or row 30 minutes at moderate intensity.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Perform a 20-minute tempo workout (5 easy, 10 comfortably hard, 5 easy).

days.title: Log

days.title: HIIT science
days.work: Learn aerobic vs. anaerobic energy systems; complete a 4-minute Tabata of squat jumps.

days.title: Shuttle runs
days.work: Complete 6×30-second shuttle runs with 90-second recovery.

days.title: Hill repeats
days.work: Run or walk 6 hill repeats, focusing on driving knees and arm swing.

days.title: Design HIIT
days.work: Design a 20-minute HIIT workout with safe work-to-rest ratios and complete it.

days.title: Check
days.work: Lead a family member through your HIIT workout and write a comparison of HIIT vs. steady state.

days.title: Pacing
days.work: Plan a pacing strategy for a 5K based on training data.

days.title: Easy run
days.work: Do a 20-minute shake-out run plus strides.

days.title: 5K
days.work: Run, walk, or bike a timed 5K (or join a community fun run).

days.title: Recovery
days.work: Complete active recovery (walk, foam rolling, stretching).

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare 5K results to week 1 mile time and update goals.

objectives: Explain muscle physiology and training principles

days.work: Learn major muscle groups and how muscles adapt; perform a bodyweight circuit.

days.title: Squat pattern
days.work: Learn bodyweight squat and goblet squat technique with video feedback.

days.title: Push pattern
days.work: Learn push-up progressions (incline to full) and band chest press.

days.title: Pull pattern
days.work: Learn band rows and inverted rows using a sturdy table.

days.title: Check
days.work: Demonstrate squat, push, and pull patterns with correct form.

days.title: Hip hinge
days.work: Learn the hip hinge with a dowel and perform Romanian deadlifts with light weight.

days.title: Lunges
days.work: Learn forward, reverse, and lateral lunges.

days.title: Step-ups
days.work: Perform step-ups and calf raises.

days.title: Lower body workout
days.work: Complete a full lower-body workout (3 sets of 10–12).

days.title: Check
days.work: Log workout and self-assess form via video.

objectives: Perform upper body and core exercises

days.title: Overhead press
days.work: Learn overhead press and lateral raises with bands or light dumbbells.

days.title: Core stability
days.work: Learn planks, side planks, dead bugs, and bird dogs.

days.title: Anti-rotation
days.work: Perform Pallof press with bands.

days.title: Upper body workout
days.work: Complete a full upper-body and core workout.

days.title: Check
days.work: Log and reflect on progress.

days.title: Program types
days.work: Compare full-body vs. split routines and choose one; complete a 25-minute bodyweight circuit.

days.title: Estimating load
days.work: Learn reps in reserve (RIR); test loads for goblet squat, row, and press to find a weight leaving 2–3 reps in reserve.

days.title: Design
days.work: Write a 4-week, 3-day-per-week full-body program with sets, reps, rest, and weekly progression.

days.title: Workout A
days.work: Complete Workout A (squat, push, hinge, core) and log loads and RPE.

days.title: Workout B & submit
days.work: Complete Workout B (lunge, pull, press, carry) and submit the written program.

objectives: Reassess muscular fitness and evaluate the program

days.title: Workout A+
days.work: Complete Workout A with a progression (added rep or load) and log it.

days.title: Retest
days.work: Retest 90° push-ups, curl-ups, and plank hold; compare with week 1.

days.title: Workout B+
days.work: Complete Workout B with progression.

days.title: Analysis

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Quiz on resistance-training principles, muscle groups, and safety.

days.title: Types of stretching
days.work: Learn static, dynamic, and PNF stretching; retest sit-and-reach.

days.title: Hip & hamstring mobility
days.work: Complete a 20-minute hip and hamstring mobility routine (90/90, pigeon, strap hamstring).

days.title: Shoulder & spine
days.work: Complete thoracic rotations, wall slides, and cat-cow; assess shoulder flexibility.

days.title: PNF with a partner
days.work: Practice contract-relax hamstring stretching with a family member.

days.title: Check
days.work: Design and perform a 15-minute personal mobility routine.

objectives: Perform foundational yoga postures with alignment

days.title: Breathing
days.work: Practice diaphragmatic and box breathing; journal stress level before and after.

days.title: Standing poses

days.title: Check
days.work: Demonstrate a 10-pose sequence with correct alignment and reflect on stress reduction.

days.title: Stress & sleep

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Quiz on flexibility and mind-body concepts and log sit-and-reach progress.

objectives: Perform forehand, backhand, serve, and dink

days.title: Dinking

days.title: Scoring & play

materials: badminton rackets and shuttles (or a community center)

days.title: Grip & clears

days.title: Footwork
days.work: Learn base position and six-corner footwork drills.

days.work: Play games focusing on moving opponents front-to-back.

days.work: Skill test and written comparison of pickleball and badminton strategy.

days.title: Aerobic retest
days.work: Retest the 1-mile run/walk and record resting heart rate.

days.title: Muscular retest
days.work: Retest push-ups, curl-ups, and trunk lift.

days.title: Flexibility retest
days.work: Retest sit-and-reach and shoulder stretch.

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Compare all results to baseline and graph progress.

days.title: Semester reflection
days.work: Write a semester reflection and revise SMART goals for spring.

days.title: Groundstrokes
days.work: Learn forehand and backhand groundstrokes and rally against a wall.

days.title: Serve
days.work: Learn the flat serve with a trophy position.

days.title: Scoring & etiquette
days.work: Learn tennis scoring and court etiquette.

days.title: Tournament
days.work: Play a round-robin of your choice of racquet sport with family or friends.

days.title: Check

days.title: Ten Essentials
days.work: Learn the Ten Essentials and pack a daypack.

days.title: Plan a hike
days.work: Use a trail app or State Parks site to plan a 3–5 mile hike; calculate time and elevation.

days.title: Conditioning

days.title: Day hike

days.title: Map reading

days.title: Compass bearings
days.work: Learn to take and follow bearings.

days.title: Pace count

days.title: Orienteering course
days.work: Complete a family-designed orienteering course with 8 control points.

days.title: Check
days.work: Navigation skills test.

objectives: Ride safely and plan active commutes

days.title: Bike safety

days.title: Traffic skills
days.work: Practice signaling, scanning, and riding in bike lanes in a safe area.

days.title: Endurance ride
days.work: Complete a 45–60 minute ride at moderate intensity.

days.title: Active commute
days.work: Map an active-transportation route to a frequent destination and ride or walk it.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a plan to replace two car trips per week with active transportation.

days.work: Learn water safety, rip currents, and reach-throw-don't-go rescues.

days.title: Strokes
days.work: Practice freestyle and backstroke technique (or hike stair intervals if no pool).

days.title: Endurance
days.work: Swim 20 minutes continuously or complete a long hike.

days.work: Practice treading water and survival floating for time.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Complete an outdoor pursuits quiz and log.

days.work: Count music in eights at different tempos and learn grapevine, step-touch, box step, and V-step.

days.work: Learn a full line dance (e.g., the Cupid Shuffle or Electric Slide) and teach it to a family member.

days.work: Perform the routine for an audience and record heart rate before and after.

days.work: Learn situational awareness and verbal de-escalation strategies; role-play setting boundaries.

days.work: Practice a balanced stance, palm-heel strike, and front kick on a pillow or pad.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Demonstrate techniques safely and complete a quiz on dance and group fitness concepts.

days.work: Practice forearm passing against a wall (target 30 consecutive) and with a partner.

days.work: Practice overhead setting with proper hand shape; 50 self-sets.

days.work: Practice underhand and overhand serves to target zones.

days.work: Skills test and a diagram of a serve-receive formation.

days.work: Practice backhand and forehand disc throws for accuracy at 10 and 20 yards.

days.title: Defense
days.work: Compare person-to-person and zone defenses and when to use each.

days.title: Game play
days.work: Play ultimate with family or a community pickup game, self-officiating under Spirit of the Game.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write an analysis of one offensive and one defensive strategy used in play.

days.title: Rules study
days.work: Study the official rules of one sport and learn its hand signals.

days.title: Officiating practice
days.work: Officiate a youth or family game (e.g., volleyball, pickleball) using correct signals.

days.title: Risk management
days.work: Identify safety hazards at a play area and write a risk-management checklist.

days.title: Plan an event

days.title: Check
days.work: Run the event or simulate it and reflect on leadership challenges.

days.work: Learn signs of overtraining and injury prevention; complete an active-recovery walk.

days.work: Read research on exercise and anxiety; complete a 30-minute moderate cardio session and rate mood before/after.

days.title: Recovery strategies

days.work: Write a recovery plan based on your sleep log.

days.title: Plan strength & flexibility
days.work: Plan strength and flexibility components; complete a strength session.

days.title: Lifetime activities

objectives: Carry out and monitor a personal fitness plan

courses.subject: ELEC
courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Design (CTE)
courses.description: A Career Technical Education course in the Engineering and Architecture sector (Engineering Design pathway). Students learn the engineering design process, technical sketching and dimensioning, precision measurement and statistics, and parametric 3D CAD modeling with free tools (Onshape for Education, Tinkercad). They reverse engineer household products, study materials and manufacturing, build and test prototypes, and finish with a semester-long capstone that solves a real problem for a real user, documented in an engineering notebook and digital portfolio.
courses.framework: California Career Technical Education Model Curriculum Standards – Engineering and Architecture Sector, Engineering Design Pathway (C) and CTE Anchor Standards

standards.CTE-EA-C1.0: Understand the history, impact, and careers of engineering design.
standards.CTE-EA-C2.1: Use the engineering design process to identify problems, generate and evaluate solutions, and document work in an engineering notebook.
standards.CTE-EA-C2.2: Define design problems with criteria and constraints and evaluate solutions with decision matrices.
standards.CTE-EA-C3.1: Produce freehand technical sketches using isometric, oblique, and multiview (orthographic) projection.
standards.CTE-EA-C3.2: Apply dimensioning standards and line conventions (ASME Y14.5 basics) to technical drawings.
standards.CTE-EA-C4.1: Use precision measuring tools (rulers, calipers) and apply units, accuracy, precision, and tolerances.
standards.CTE-EA-C4.2: Apply statistical analysis (mean, median, standard deviation) to measurement and quality data.
standards.CTE-EA-C5.1: Create parametric 3D solid models of parts using computer-aided design (CAD) software.
standards.CTE-EA-C5.2: Create CAD assemblies with constraints/mates and generate working drawings from 3D models.
standards.CTE-EA-C6.1: Reverse engineer a product to analyze its function, structure, materials, and manufacturing processes.
standards.CTE-EA-C7.1: Select appropriate materials based on mechanical properties, cost, and sustainability.
standards.CTE-EA-C7.2: Describe manufacturing processes (additive, subtractive, forming) and build and test prototypes safely.
standards.CTE-EA-C8.1: Apply human factors, ergonomics, and user-centered design to product development.
standards.CTE-EA-C9.1: Communicate design solutions through technical reports, presentations, and portfolios.
standards.CTE-ANCHOR-2.0: Communications: acquire and accurately use sector terminology and communicate in oral, written, and multimedia formats.
standards.CTE-ANCHOR-5.0: Problem Solving and Critical Thinking: conduct short and sustained projects using critical and creative thinking, logical reasoning, and analysis.
standards.CTE-ANCHOR-6.0: Health and Safety: demonstrate health and safety procedures, regulations, and personal health practices in the workplace.
standards.CTE-ANCHOR-8.0: Ethics and Legal Responsibilities: practice professional, ethical, and legal behavior, including intellectual property.
standards.CTE-ANCHOR-9.0: Leadership and Teamwork: work with peers to promote divergent and creative perspectives, effective leadership, and group dynamics.
standards.CTE-ANCHOR-10.0: Technical Knowledge and Skills: apply essential technical knowledge and skills common to the sector, following procedures when carrying out experiments or tasks.
standards.CTE-ANCHOR-11.0: Demonstration and Application: demonstrate and apply knowledge and skills in classroom, laboratory, and workplace settings.

units.title: The Engineering Design Process and Careers
units.big_idea: Engineers solve problems through an iterative, documented design process.

units.title: Technical Sketching and Drawing
units.big_idea: Sketches and drawings are the universal language engineers use to communicate ideas precisely.

units.title: Measurement and Statistics
units.big_idea: Precise measurement and statistical analysis ensure parts fit and products are consistent.

units.title: Computer-Aided Design (CAD)
units.big_idea: Parametric CAD lets engineers model, modify, and document designs quickly.

units.title: Reverse Engineering
units.big_idea: Taking products apart reveals the design decisions behind them.

units.title: Materials, Manufacturing, and Prototyping
units.big_idea: Material choice and manufacturing process determine a product's cost, performance, and sustainability.

units.title: User-Centered Design and Ergonomics
units.big_idea: Good design starts with the people who will use it.

units.title: Ethics, Sustainability, and Intellectual Property
units.big_idea: Engineers have responsibilities to the public, the environment, and other inventors.

units.title: Capstone Design Project
units.big_idea: A complete design cycle—from problem to tested prototype—shows mastery of engineering design.

days.title: Engineering careers
days.work: Research five engineering disciplines (mechanical, civil, electrical, biomedical, industrial) and record salary, education, and a California employer for each.

days.title: Engineering notebook
days.work: Set up a bound engineering notebook with table of contents, dated entries, and signing conventions.

days.title: Design that changed the world
days.work: Read about an innovation (e.g., the Golden Gate Bridge, the iPhone) and summarize the problem it solved.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Watch or conduct an interview with a practicing engineer and record five takeaways.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a 300-word career reflection and submit the notebook for a format check.

days.title: Design process model
days.work: Learn the steps (define, research, ideate, select, prototype, test, iterate, communicate) and diagram them in the notebook.

days.title: Design brief
days.work: Write a design brief for a paper bridge spanning 20 cm with limited materials.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Sketch five bridge ideas in 15 minutes and select one with a decision matrix.

days.title: Build & test
days.work: Build the bridge and test load with pennies; record results.

days.title: Iterate & check
days.work: Redesign once, retest, and write a reflection on what changed.

days.title: Lab safety
days.work: Learn shop safety rules, PPE, and tool handling; pass a safety quiz.

days.title: Marshmallow challenge
days.work: Complete the spaghetti-marshmallow tower challenge with family members and reflect on teamwork.

days.title: Project management
days.work: Learn Gantt charts and build one for a hypothetical project.

days.title: Documentation
days.work: Practice writing a test procedure and data table.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Unit 1 quiz on design process and careers.

days.title: Line work
days.work: Practice horizontal, vertical, and angled lines and construction lines.

days.title: Circles & arcs
days.work: Sketch circles and arcs using boxes and diagonals.

days.title: Proportion
days.work: Sketch household objects using proportional estimation.

days.title: Thumbnail sketches
days.work: Create 10 thumbnail sketches of a single object from different views.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit a sketch portfolio.

objectives: Create isometric and oblique sketches of real objects

days.title: Isometric axes
days.work: Learn the 30° isometric axes and sketch three stacked-block shapes on isometric grid paper.

days.title: Isometric practice
days.work: Sketch 8 objects (stapler, phone stand, LEGO builds) isometrically, starting from a bounding box.

days.title: Isometric circles
days.work: Use the four-center method to sketch isometric ellipses, then sketch a mug and a cylinder with a hole.

days.title: Oblique sketching
days.work: Create cavalier and cabinet oblique sketches of five objects and compare their distortion.

days.title: Check
days.work: Sketch the same object in isometric and oblique for a scored quiz.

objectives: Create multiview drawings with correct alignment and line types
materials: clear plastic box or shoebox (glass-box model)

days.title: Glass box
days.work: Place a block inside a clear box, trace each face, and unfold it to see how standard views align.

days.title: Three views
days.work: Sketch front, top, and right-side views of 6 block models, choosing the most descriptive front view.

days.title: Hidden & center lines
days.work: Add hidden lines and center lines to drawings of parts with holes and slots.

days.title: Visualization
days.work: Match 12 isometric pictorials to their multiview drawings and sketch the missing view in 6 problems.

days.title: Check
days.work: Multiview quiz: draw three views of an unseen object from an isometric.

materials: sample part (e.g., a LEGO brick or bracket)

days.title: Dimensioning rules
days.work: Learn line types and ASME basics (no double dimensions, dimension features in their most descriptive view).

days.title: Practice
days.work: Fully dimension multiview drawings of three block parts.

days.title: Holes & arcs
days.work: Dimension holes, radii, and counterbores using leaders and notes.

days.title: Tolerances
days.work: Learn limit and plus/minus tolerances and calculate fits between a peg and a hole.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Unit 2 test: produce a fully dimensioned multiview drawing of a household part.

days.title: Accuracy vs. precision
days.work: Use target diagrams and a measurement game to distinguish accuracy and precision.

days.title: Ruler reading
days.work: Measure 10 objects to 1/16 inch and 1 mm, converting between units.

days.title: Calipers
days.work: Learn to zero and read a caliper for outside, inside, and depth measurements; measure 10 coins.

days.title: Measure a part
days.work: Measure all features of a LEGO brick and sketch it fully dimensioned.

days.title: Check
days.work: Measurement practical with a scored data sheet.

objectives: Calculate descriptive statistics for measurement data

days.title: Data collection
days.work: Measure the length of 50 'identical' items and record in a spreadsheet.

days.title: Central tendency
days.work: Calculate mean, median, mode, and range by hand and with spreadsheet functions.

days.title: Standard deviation
days.work: Calculate standard deviation and explain what it reveals about manufacturing consistency.

days.title: Histograms
days.work: Create a histogram and assess whether the data is approximately normal.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a quality-control report recommending whether the batch meets a given tolerance.

objectives: Calculate area, volume, mass, and density for parts

days.title: Area & volume
days.work: Calculate volume and surface area of prisms, cylinders, and composite parts from drawings.

days.title: Density lab
days.work: Find the density of three materials using water displacement and a kitchen scale.

days.title: Mass estimates
days.work: Predict part mass from volume and material density and verify by weighing.

days.title: Review
days.work: Mixed review of measurement, statistics, and geometry problems.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Unit 3 test.

materials: computer with Onshape for Education (free) and Tinkercad

days.title: Tinkercad warm-up
days.work: Build a keychain in Tinkercad using primitive shapes and holes.

days.title: Onshape setup
days.work: Create an Onshape education account and complete the interface tutorial.

days.title: Sketch & extrude
days.work: Create constrained 2D sketches and extrude them into a block with holes.

days.title: Constraints
days.work: Practice fully constraining sketches with dimensions and geometric relations.

days.title: Check
days.work: Model a dimensioned block part from Unit 2 in Onshape.

objectives: Use revolve, fillet, chamfer, shell, and pattern features

days.title: Revolve
days.work: Model a bottle or knob using a revolve feature.

days.title: Fillets & chamfers
days.work: Add fillets and chamfers and explain why designers soften edges.

days.title: Shell
days.work: Shell a box to create a hollow enclosure with uniform wall thickness.

days.title: Patterns
days.work: Use linear and circular patterns to model a phone stand with vents.

days.title: Check
days.work: Model a three-feature part from a working drawing.

days.title: Design intent
days.work: Learn how to plan a feature tree that captures design intent.

days.title: Measure
days.work: Measure a household object (e.g., a bottle opener) with calipers.

days.title: Model
days.work: Model the object in Onshape from your measurements.

days.title: Modify
days.work: Change a key dimension and verify the model updates correctly.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit the model and a reflection on design intent.

days.title: Assembly basics
days.work: Insert parts into an Onshape assembly and fix the base part.

days.title: Mates
days.work: Apply fastened, revolute, and slider mates to model a simple hinge.

days.title: Degrees of freedom
days.work: Analyze remaining degrees of freedom and animate the mechanism.

days.title: Interference
days.work: Check for interference and fix problems.

days.title: Check
days.work: Build a 4-part assembly (e.g., a toy car with axles and wheels).

objectives: Generate working drawings from CAD models

days.title: Drawings
days.work: Create a drawing from a part with standard views.

days.title: Dimensions
days.work: Add dimensions and notes following standards.

days.title: Section views
days.work: Create a section view of a hollow part.

days.title: Assembly drawing
days.work: Create an exploded assembly drawing with a bill of materials.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Unit 4 CAD practical: model and draw a part from a sketch.

objectives: Analyze a product's function and structure

days.title: Why reverse engineer
days.work: Learn legitimate uses of reverse engineering and safety for disassembly.

days.title: Observation
days.work: Document the product's function with a black-box diagram of inputs and outputs.

days.title: Disassembly
days.work: Disassemble the product, photographing and labeling each step.

days.title: Parts list
days.work: Create a parts list with quantities, materials, and functions.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit the reverse engineering notebook entries.

days.title: Measure parts
days.work: Measure two key parts with calipers.

days.title: CAD
days.work: Model the two parts in Onshape.

days.title: Material & process
days.work: Identify the material and likely manufacturing process for each part.

days.title: Redesign
days.work: Propose an improvement with sketches and justification.

days.title: Check
days.work: Reassemble the product and submit a reverse engineering report.

days.title: Review: sketching
days.work: Mixed practice on isometric and multiview sketching.

days.title: Review: measurement
days.work: Practice measurement and statistics problems.

days.title: Review: CAD
days.work: Practice CAD modeling of a review part.

days.title: Semester exam part 1
days.work: Written exam on design process, sketching, and statistics.

days.title: Semester exam part 2
days.work: CAD and sketching practical.

materials: samples of wood, aluminum foil, plastic, cardboard

days.title: Material families
days.work: Classify common household items by material family (metals, polymers, ceramics, composites).

days.title: Properties
days.work: Learn mechanical properties and test bending stiffness of wood, plastic, and metal strips with weights.

days.title: Tensile test
days.work: Test tensile strength of string, yarn, and fishing line by adding weights until failure.

days.title: Selection
days.work: Use an Ashby-style chart to choose a material for a bike frame and a water bottle.

days.title: Check
days.work: Material selection quiz and lab report.

objectives: Describe additive, subtractive, and forming processes

days.title: Processes overview
days.work: Watch videos of injection molding, CNC milling, and casting; take notes.

days.title: Additive manufacturing
days.work: Learn 3D printing and prepare an STL file for printing.

days.title: Design for manufacturing
days.work: Identify draft angles and wall thickness in molded parts.

days.title: Local manufacturing
days.work: Research a California manufacturer and their processes.

days.title: Check
days.work: Quiz on manufacturing.

materials: cardboard, hot glue, foam board, craft knife, cutting mat
3D printer at a library makerspace (if available)

days.title: Prototype types
days.work: Compare low- and high-fidelity prototypes using examples from IDEO and product teardown videos; review craft-knife and hot-glue safety.

days.title: Cardboard mock-up
days.work: Build a full-size cardboard mock-up of a phone or tablet stand and test viewing angle with your device.

days.title: CAD refinement
days.work: Update the stand in Onshape based on what the mock-up revealed (angle, cable slot, stability).

days.title: Print or build
days.work: Export an STL and print at a library makerspace, or build a refined version from foam board using the CAD drawing as a template.

days.title: Check
days.work: Photograph both prototypes and write a notebook entry comparing time, cost, and what each revealed.

objectives: Write and run a test plan

days.title: Test plan
days.work: Write a test plan for the stand with measurable success criteria (holds 300 g, angle 60°±5°, no tipping at a 10° table tilt).

days.title: Testing
days.work: Run five trials of each test and record results in a data table.

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Calculate mean and standard deviation for each test and identify the most likely failure mode.

days.title: Iterate
days.work: Modify the design to address the failure mode, rebuild, and retest.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Unit 6 test on materials, manufacturing processes, and prototyping.

days.title: Ergonomics
days.work: Compare well and poorly designed tools (scissors, can openers, peelers) and list ergonomic features.

days.title: Anthropometry
days.work: Measure hand length, grip diameter, and reach for five people and compare to published percentile tables.

days.title: Design for range
days.work: Use 5th–95th percentile data to size a handle for a garden tool.

days.title: Accessibility
days.work: Study universal design principles and evaluate a product for users with limited hand strength.

days.title: Check
days.work: Redesign a handle in CAD using anthropometric data and justify the dimensions.

days.title: Empathy
days.work: Learn the design thinking empathize stage and watch a user-research example video.

days.title: Interview guide
days.work: Write 10 open-ended interview questions about a daily frustration (e.g., organizing a backpack or kitchen).

days.title: Interviews
days.work: Interview three people and record notes and direct quotes.

days.title: Synthesis
days.work: Cluster findings on sticky notes and create a persona and journey map.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write three 'How might we...' needs statements.

objectives: Communicate design ideas visually and orally

days.title: Rendering
days.work: Create appearance-styled renderings of your phone stand in Onshape.

days.title: Storyboard
days.work: Create a 6-panel storyboard showing a user's experience with the product.

days.title: Pitch writing
days.work: Write a 60-second elevator pitch covering problem, user, solution, and evidence.

days.title: Practice
days.work: Record and revise the pitch twice.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Deliver the pitch and take a short Unit 7 quiz.

objectives: Analyze engineering failures and ethical codes

days.title: Code of ethics
days.work: Read the NSPE Code of Ethics and summarize its fundamental canons.

days.title: Case study 1
days.work: Analyze the Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapse and identify the design failure.

days.title: Case study 2
days.work: Analyze the Challenger disaster and the engineers' ethical dilemma.

days.title: Factor of safety
days.work: Calculate factors of safety for a shelf bracket and discuss why they matter.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a 500-word ethics case analysis.

days.title: Life cycle
days.work: Map the life cycle (materials, manufacturing, use, disposal) of a plastic water bottle and estimate its impact.

days.title: Design for sustainability
days.work: Redesign a disposable product for disassembly and recycling.

days.title: Intellectual property
days.work: Learn the differences among patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets.

days.title: Patent search
days.work: Search Google Patents for prior art related to a product idea and read one patent's claims.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Unit 8 quiz on ethics, sustainability, and IP.

objectives: Identify a real problem and user

days.title: Problem hunting
days.work: List 15 problems observed at home or in the community and select three candidates.

days.title: User interviews
days.work: Interview at least two potential users for each of the top candidates.

days.title: Selection
days.work: Use a decision matrix to select the capstone problem based on impact and feasibility.

days.title: Design brief
days.work: Write a design brief with client, problem statement, criteria, and constraints.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit the design brief and a Gantt chart for weeks 28–36.

objectives: Research existing solutions and relevant science

days.title: Existing products
days.work: Find and benchmark five existing solutions on price, features, and weaknesses.

days.title: Patent search
days.work: Search for related patents and summarize two.

days.title: Technical research
days.work: Research the science or engineering principles your solution will depend on.

days.title: Specifications
days.work: Write measurable design specifications from your criteria.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit research summary with citations.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Generate at least 20 ideas using brainstorming and SCAMPER.

days.title: Concept sketches
days.work: Develop three concepts into annotated isometric sketches.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Get feedback on the three concepts from your user.

days.title: Selection
days.work: Select a final concept with a weighted decision matrix.

days.title: Check
days.work: Present the selected concept and justification.

objectives: Model the final design in CAD

days.title: Part modeling
days.work: Model all custom parts in Onshape.

days.title: Assembly
days.work: Assemble parts with mates and check for interference.

days.title: Drawings
days.work: Create dimensioned working drawings for each part.

days.title: Bill of materials
days.work: Create a bill of materials with sourcing and cost.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit CAD files, drawings, and BOM for design review.

objectives: Plan fabrication and build the main structure safely

days.title: Fabrication plan
days.work: Write a step-by-step build plan listing tools, safety hazards, and PPE for each step.

days.title: Materials prep
days.work: Gather materials, set up a safe workspace, and mark and cut stock from the working drawings.

days.title: Main structure
days.work: Fabricate the main structure or housing and check critical dimensions with calipers.

days.title: Custom parts
days.work: Send parts to a makerspace 3D printer or hand-fabricate custom components.

days.title: Progress check
days.work: Photograph progress, log hours and costs against the BOM, and update the Gantt chart.

objectives: Complete and assemble a functional prototype

days.title: Remaining parts
days.work: Finish fabricating remaining parts and deburr or sand edges for safety.

days.title: Fit check
days.work: Dry-fit all parts and measure clearances; record any parts that do not meet tolerance.

days.title: Rework
days.work: Rework or reprint out-of-tolerance parts and update the CAD model to match changes.

days.title: Final assembly
days.work: Assemble the full prototype and verify it operates as intended.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit an as-built drawing update and a notebook entry describing build problems and solutions.

days.title: Test plan
days.work: Write a test procedure for each design specification with pass/fail criteria.

days.title: Testing
days.work: Run at least five trials per test and record data in a spreadsheet with mean and standard deviation.

days.title: User testing
days.work: Have your user try the prototype while you observe; record quotes and pain points.

days.title: Iterate
days.work: Make at least one evidence-based design improvement.

days.title: Retest
days.work: Retest the changed feature and summarize whether each specification is now met.

days.title: Report outline
days.work: Outline the report: executive summary, problem, research, concept selection, design, testing, conclusions, and citations.

days.title: Report draft
days.work: Write the full technical report draft (2,000+ words) with figures and data tables.

days.title: Portfolio
days.work: Build a digital portfolio page with renderings, drawings, build photos, and test graphs.

days.title: Revision
days.work: Revise the report for clarity and correct technical terminology; check all sources are cited.

days.title: Submit
days.work: Submit the final report and publish the portfolio.

objectives: Present the capstone to a panel

days.title: Rehearsal
days.work: Build a 10-minute slide presentation and rehearse it twice with timing.

days.title: Panel presentation
days.work: Present to a panel of family and community members (ideally including an engineer) and demonstrate the prototype.

days.title: Q&A follow-up
days.work: Write responses to the panel's questions and list next steps if the product were developed further.

days.title: Career pathway plan
days.work: Research community college and university engineering programs in California and write a pathway plan.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the written final covering the design process, drawing, measurement, CAD, materials, and ethics.
